falcon_scope: Falcon process-launch telemetry (ProcessRollup2) from the same test host was queried read-only with each Falcon-convertible rule's converted LogScale query, scoped to that host, in every success window. These are query matches, not Falcon alerts, and Falcon isn't noise-checked. Rules that don't convert to LogScale show the conversion failure.

notes.0f3109b3-d7e5-4c8a-a082-d8f0fa7be7a1: Its scope also takes setegid and setregid; they aren't measured, for hits or noise: the test host's capture didn't subscribe to those events, so the stores hold none.
notes.11ac0458-e527-4568-8205-243ebed6fd8c: Elastic EQL (an EQL sequence, as Kibana deploys it) and ClickHouse (windowFunnel) enforce its order; Splunk runs its temporal (unordered) fallback, ES|QL can't convert temporal_ordered, and OpenSearch has no correlations. In the 18:58 run the stores' events came in the rule's order, for one host and user, within its 15m timespan: download (curl) at 18:58:21.889, credential capture (osascript at 18:58:21.927, dscl at 18:58:25.187), then staging (ditto) at 18:58:25.469; it fires there on Elastic EQL, Splunk and ClickHouse. In the 05:29 run the download came last, so only Splunk's unordered fallback fires there. On Falcon, its first step's base rule (terminal_or_scripteditor_download_exec) matched once in the 18:58 window; in the earlier windows some of its matches were the run harness's own SSM wrapper (`echo … | base64 -D` as root), not the simulation. The correlation itself doesn't convert to LogScale. Its group-by user.name drops the root-run LaunchDaemon branch (the ditto branch is unaffected).
notes.18d6dc1e-8440-4894-9f48-988bf438b694: Its file_event scope also takes renames into these paths. Renames reach the stores only where the collector's filter keeps them (23 in all the replayed hours), so rename coverage, and rename noise, are measured only that far.
notes.46423852-c12c-4e9a-bb3e-0b4ad213b684: Fires in both npm runs. Its agent-config step is file_event and also takes renames: renames into ~/Library/LaunchAgents reach the stores where the collector's filter keeps them (23 in all the replayed hours), but the coreSigma collector drops renames into the agent-config and /Library/Caches/com.apple. paths, so that half of the scope isn't covered by collected data.

windows_note: The npm simulation ran twice: at 05:42, and at 16:55 with the shipped atomic. Its verdicts reproduce: the same rules fire on every store and on Falcon in both runs. The paste-to-stealer simulation also ran twice: at 05:29 with the download step last, and at 18:58 in the real ClickFix order (download, prompt and dscl, then ditto). The 16:55 and 18:58 runs' unified log captures are Info-level. On 2026-11-12 the paste-to-stealer and npm simulations ran again with revised atomics (launch items and a stealer stub in the home directory; node creating the settings file itself), and two new ones ran: an SSH key login to localhost and a writable-and-executable memory request. From about 14:37 UTC that day the test host's unified log stream used the collector's own predicate, and eslogger subscribed to the collector's event list. On the evening of 2026-11-12 (from 21:25 UTC) 21 more simulations ran, one atomic per rule; 20 completed, and an account create-and-delete timed out when its dscl delete waited on a TCC prompt. Seven of them, the timed-out one and six that ran beside unrelated activity on the host (a Screen Sharing session, sudo commands and a TCC prompt answered by hand), ran again from 23:34 UTC, with the account deletes moved to cleanup; the originals are marked superseded and don't count. On 2026-11-13 (from 04:03 UTC) four more ran: a firewall toggle, a refused `csrutil disable`, a run of a binary whose signature no longer matches, and a file deletion in /private/etc. Later on 2026-11-13 (from 14:51 UTC) three more ran: the Gatekeeper staging chain with a keychain partition-list change as its third step, perl signalling a dummy process, and failed lookups on a throwaway keychain. Then three hands-on windows (15:55 to 16:19 UTC): a Screen Sharing connection, Open Anyway for a quarantined test app, and Run in Script Editor, each done by hand and counted only for its own rule (the window's `rules` list), so other activity in it verifies nothing else. Two earlier Screen Sharing windows are superseded: no connection started in the first (15:20), and the second's run (15:50) was interrupted. Every success window ends before its cleanup starts: the earlier ones were trimmed to 1 ms before the run script writes its cleanup file, and the reruns' windows come from the host's clock and end before the cleanup.
